I don't have access to the latest news and updates. however, i can provide some insights on how tax laws generally affect deductions for small businesses. 

recent changes in tax laws may affect deductions for small businesses in different ways, depending on the specific changes. for example, the tax cuts and jobs act of 2017 introduced several changes that could affect small business deductions, including:

1. changes to depreciation rules: the law increased the amount of assets that can be expensed under section 179, and also introduced a new bonus depreciation provision, which allows businesses to immediately deduct the full cost of certain assets.

2. changes to qualified business income deduction: the law introduced a new deduction for pass-through businesses, which allows these businesses to deduct up to 20% of their qualified business income from their taxable income.

3. changes to entertainment expenses: the law eliminated the deduction for entertainment expenses, but retained the deduction for employee meals.

overall, these changes could have a significant impact on small business deductions, depending on the size and type of business. it is important for small business owners to stay informed of any changes to tax laws and work with a tax professional to ensure they are taking advantage of all available deductions.

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_007_BEGIN -->
Sure, I can definitely provide some tips on how to keep track of business expenses throughout the year so that you are prepared come tax season. Here are a few suggestions:

1. Separate business and personal expenses: Keep all business expenses separate from personal expenses to make it easier to track and categorize them. This can be done by having a separate bank account and credit card for business expenses.

2. Keep organized records: Keep receipts, invoices, and other records organized and in one place. This can be done through traditional paper files or digital systems such as accounting software or spreadsheets.

3. Use technology: There are many tools and apps available to help with expense tracking, such as Expensify or QuickBooks Self-Employed.

4. Schedule regular time to update records: Set aside time each week or month to update your records and categorize expenses. This can help avoid a last-minute scramble come tax season.

5. Hire a professional: Consider hiring a tax professional to help with bookkeeping and tax preparation, as they can help ensure that everything is recorded accurately and in compliance with tax laws.

By following these tips, you should be able to keep track of your business expenses throughout the year, making tax season less stressful, and providing you the confidence that you have identified as many deductions as possible.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_007_END -->
